_comment: Poughkeepsie ADDENDUM — Doug Phillips Park, Fishkill NY. Found 2026-08-04 while auditing why the main batch published only 9 of its 12 verified rows. The Town of Fishkill's 4/24/2024 project status report funded BOTH halves of one project: 2 courts at Maurer-Geering (which the main batch carried as `verified` and which are still not built — demoted to probable 2026-08-04) and 6 NEW courts at Doug Phillips Park, which opened 2024-06-12 and which the directory did not have at all. Separate batch, not an edit to poughkeepsie.json, because --stage=listings INSERTs every row in its artifact unconditionally: re-running it against the 18-row config would duplicate the whole metro. A separate batch also gives this row its own one-statement rollback handle.
_no_spreadsheet_comment: No spreadsheet_id: this venue has no research workbook. It was found inside a municipal source cited by another row and researched directly, so the artifact was hand-built rather than extracted by scripts/lib/workbook-extract.mjs. spreadsheet_id is provenance only — the importer never reads it.
_envelope_comment: Identical to poughkeepsie.json — same MSA, derived from the Dutchess + Orange county boundary boxes rather than from the observed venue bbox. Doug Phillips Park (41.544245, -73.8650681) sits well inside it.
_expected_publish_comment: 1 publish, 0 hold. The coordinate is high precision (leisure/park way/469770262 "Doug Phillips Park", matched on the name+city rung), access_type is public, and research_status is verified on the Town's own ribbon-cutting announcement — so nothing in the gate can hold it. require_all_geocoded is deliberately TRUE here, unlike the main config: a single-row batch with no coordinate has nothing to import, so a geocode miss should abort rather than quietly land a permanent draft.
